run.question: We're running low on disk space. Can you check our application indexes (app-187-*) and identify which one is consuming the most storage? Please tell me the index name and approximately how much space it's using.

report.summary: Of the 21 indices matching app-187-*, the largest by storage is app-187-metrics-analytics at approximately 508.3 KB (primary and total store size both 508.3 KB), holding 5,000 documents and reporting green health (evidence ff01cd18-b207-4a92-adc8-1ed7a4cde476-t0:c83d0b25-91e4-46fb-abc9-909dc0e3c50d, confirmed by 302c24ed-92de-4b52-96bb-8e044a040e9c-t0:4ac0e979-b65a-4d00-afe5-8d91791091ff). It is roughly two orders of magnitude larger than any other app-187-* index: the remaining 20 are app-187-logs-01 through app-187-logs-20, each holding 10 documents and reporting a store size of 9 KB (9.1 KB for app-187-logs-01) with yellow health. All 21 indices are open, and repeating the listing with expand_wildcards=all returned the same 21 indices, so no closed or hidden app-187-* index appeared in either listing. Two limits on this answer: the index listing tool has no time range and reports the cluster at the moment of the query (2026-11-21T05:03:14 and 05:03:17), which is after the authorized window 2026-11-20T05:03:12 to 2026-11-21T05:03:12, so these sizes are not shown to have been the same during the incident window; and nothing observed here measures node or volume free space, so the 'running low on disk' premise is not confirmed or ranked by this evidence. No root cause is assigned: this is a capacity-ranking question, not a diagnosed fault, and naming the largest index as a cause of disk pressure would be a causal claim the sizes alone do not support.

claims.text: app-187-metrics-analytics is the largest index matching app-187-*: store.size 508.3 KB and pri.store.size 508.3 KB, docs.count 5000, status open, health green, listed first in a listing sorted by store.size descending.
The other 20 matching indices are app-187-logs-01 through app-187-logs-20, each with docs.count 10 and store.size 9 KB (app-187-logs-01 reports 9.1 KB), status open and health yellow.

The pattern app-187-* returned 21 indices with indices_shown 21 and indices_omitted 0, and a repeat listing with expand_wildcards=all returned the same 21 indices, so both listings are complete for that pattern as queried.

In absolute terms none of the app-187-* indices is large: the biggest is 508.3 KB and every other one is 9 KB or 9.1 KB, so these indices against an unspecified disk do not by themselves demonstrate the reported disk shortage, and the storage pressure is not attributable to a single multi-gigabyte application index in this data.

If growth rather than absolute size is the concern, app-187-metrics-analytics is the candidate to watch because it carries 5000 documents versus 10 in each log index, which is consistent with continued ingestion, but no time-series of index size was available in this Run to test a growth rate.

Confirm the actual disk-pressure target before acting: check node and volume free space (for example filesystem metrics on the Elasticsearch hosts) and whether app-187-metrics-analytics is subject to an ILM/rollover or retention policy, since a 508.3 KB index is unlikely to be the driver.

gaps: elasticsearch_list_indices has no time range: the sizes and document counts are the cluster state at 2026-11-21T05:03:14 and 2026-11-21T05:03:17, after the authorized window (2026-11-20T05:03:12 to 2026-11-21T05:03:12), so index sizes during the window are unknown.

No shard-level, per-node, filesystem or volume-capacity metric was obtained. A get_metric_names query for {__name__=~".*disk.*|.*filesystem.*|.*fs_.*"} returned status error with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (operation c4574dcc-cb91-4468-9df0-a56497d264ec-t0), so disk free space and index growth over time are unchecked, not shown to be absent.
Why the 20 app-187-logs-* indices report yellow health (for example unassigned replicas) was not investigated, because it does not bear on storage ranking in the evidence gathered.
No source for index size history or growth rate was available, so a growth-based ranking cannot be made and the hypothesis about app-187-metrics-analytics growth is untested.
next_steps: Query Elasticsearch _cat/allocation, _cat/shards and _cluster/stats (or node filesystem metrics) to see whether disk pressure comes from shards, replicas or non-application indices rather than from app-187-* data.
Retrieve index size over time (for example _cat/indices snapshots or an index-size metric) to distinguish a large-but-static index from a fast-growing one.
Check retention/ILM configuration for app-187-metrics-analytics and the app-187-logs-* indices to see whether 5000-document analytics data is expected to persist.
